claims: Geomagnetic storms are major disturbances in Earth's magnetosphere caused by solar wind energy transfer, typically from coronal mass ejections (CMEs) or high-speed streams.
Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are large clouds of plasma and magnetic fields ejected from the sun.
Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) can take 18 hours to several days to arrive.
High-speed streams (HSS) and co-rotating interaction regions (CIRs) can trigger geomagnetic storms.
The southward directed solar wind magnetic field interacts with Earth’s magnetic field.
Geomagnetic storms consist of an initial phase (sudden commencement).
The main phase of geomagnetic storms lasts 2-8 hours.
The recovery phase of geomagnetic storms can last up to 7 days.
NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center uses a G1-G5 scale.
A G4 (Severe) geomagnetic storm was observed on Jan 19, 2026.
A G2 (Moderate) geomagnetic storm watch was issued on March 18, 2026.
A solar storm in January 2026 included a G4-level event on Jan 19, 2026.
The January 2026 solar storm resulted from an X-class flare.
A G2 (Moderate) storm watch was issued following CMEs released on March 16, 2026.
